page.description: KaOS editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An independent, from-scratch Linux distribution built around Qt and KDE Plasma, with a rolling release, one architecture and, since 2026, the Dinit init system.
pros: KDE Plasma and Qt are the whole point, not an add-on.
Rolling release: an update gives the latest, no reinstall.
One ISO and one architecture, so there is nothing to choose.
Built from scratch, without a Debian or Arch base.
cons: Small repository: packages outside KDE and Qt are limited.
Dinit replaced systemd in 2026, so older guides do not match.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for KaOS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick, boot it and install. Writing erases the stick; the installer partitions or erases the target disk.
